newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 4.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:

* Senate Commerce Committee chairman John McCain said Monday he plans to introduce legislation requiring the sale of the TV spectra between channels 60 and 69. President Clinton's administration also is expected to propose in its federal budget later this week an auction of channels 60-69. The administration said last year that it expected to raise $5 billion from the sale of the TV spectra.

* The Korea Fair Trade Commission recently launched a formal investigation into five top U.S. film distributors for alleged anti-competitive practices. Under investigation are the Seoul branches of Sony's Columbia TriStar, News Corp's 20th Century Fox, Time Warner's Warner Bros, Walt Disney's Buena Vista and United Intl. Pictures, which jointly account for some 60 percent of the domestic market.

* Family Channel Pictures has closed down after about a year of development under president Barry Sabath, sources said Monday. The division already had eight projects in development and had spent between $1 million and $2 million. Family Channel Pictures was overseen by MTM, which is a division along with the Family Channel of parent company International Family Entertainment.

* Spider-Man is closer to becoming a motion picture as a settlement of disputes between bankrupt Carolco Pictures, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc, Canal Plus and Marvel Entertainment awaits final court approval.
* February foreign box office sales for Ron Howard's "Ransom" garnered $11.1 million, climbed to $98.9 million and is expected to top $100 million Tuesday.

* The Broadway and West End productions of Andrew Lloyd Webber's "Sunset Boulevard" will not recoup their $10 million capitalizations when each closes this spring. The shutterings were made official in separate announcements Monday.
